title: Should a Crawl Space Be Insulated?
h1: Should a Crawl Space Be Insulated, and Does It Affect Air Quality?
description: Most crawl spaces benefit from insulation, but where it goes depends on whether the space is vented or sealed. Learn the options and the air quality impact.
quick_answer: Usually, yes. In a vented crawl space, insulate the floor above it, between the joists, and insulate any ducts and pipes down there. In a sealed or encapsulated crawl space, insulate the foundation walls instead. Pair insulation with air sealing and a ground vapor barrier, because that's what keeps damp, musty crawl space air out of your home.
body:
Why insulate a crawl space in a mild climate?

San Diego winters are mild, but inland nights still get cold, and a raised floor over an open crawl space can feel chilly underfoot. Insulation helps keep floors warmer in winter and cuts heat gain on hot inland summer days. If ducts run through the crawl space, insulating them keeps the air you paid to heat or cool from losing temperature on the way to each room.

Comfort and energy aren't the only reasons. How the crawl space is insulated and sealed also affects the air you breathe upstairs.

How does a crawl space affect indoor air quality?

Air moves upward through a house. As warm air escapes through the attic and upper levels, replacement air gets pulled in from below, including from the crawl space. That air comes in through gaps around plumbing, wiring, ducts and floor registers.

If the crawl space is damp, moldy or home to rodents, some of that ends up in your living space as musty odors, mold spores and allergens. Leaky ducts in the crawl space make it worse, since return ducts can pull crawl space air directly into the system.

Where should crawl space insulation go?

It depends on how the crawl space is built:

Crawl space typeWhere to insulateAlso needed
Vented (open foundation vents)Underside of the floor, between joistsGround vapor barrier, insulated ducts and pipes, air sealing of the floor
Sealed or encapsulatedFoundation walls and rim joistsSealed liner on the ground and walls, humidity control

Mixing the two approaches, like sealing the vents but insulating only the floor, can trap moisture and cause problems. Pick one strategy and do it fully.

How do you tell what type you have?

Look at the outside of the foundation. Small screened openings spaced along the base of the walls are foundation vents, which means a vented crawl space. If the vents have been closed off and the ground and walls inside are covered with a sealed plastic liner, the space has been encapsulated. Many older homes in San Diego County have vented crawl spaces, often with original fiberglass batts that have sagged or fallen over the years.

What type of insulation works best?

  • Fiberglass batts between floor joists are common in vented crawl spaces. They need proper supports so they don't sag or fall, and they must stay dry. Wet batts lose their value and can grow mold.
  • Rigid foam board works well on foundation walls in sealed crawl spaces, since it doesn't absorb water.
  • Spray foam can insulate and air seal rim joists and irregular areas at the same time.
  • Duct insulation wraps any ducts in the crawl space, along with sealing joints first.

What should you do before insulating?

  1. Fix moisture problems. Correct drainage, repair leaks and address any mold first.
  2. Remove damaged insulation. Fallen, wet or rodent-contaminated batts should come out.
  3. Lay a vapor barrier over exposed soil.
  4. Seal the floor. Close gaps around pipes, wires and ducts that pass into the house.
  5. Seal the ducts. Leaky ducts are a direct path for crawl space air into your system.
  6. Block pest entry so new insulation doesn't become a nest.

Is crawl space insulation worth it?

For most homes with a crawl space, yes, especially if you have cold floors, ducts under the house or musty odors indoors. The biggest gains often come from doing it together with air sealing and moisture control, not insulation alone.

If you're replacing old batts anyway, it's also a good moment to look over the plumbing, ducts and framing while everything is exposed. Small leaks and rodent entry points are much easier to spot and fix before new insulation goes up.

faqs: Should I insulate the floor or the walls of my crawl space?

If your crawl space has open foundation vents, insulate the floor above it between the joists. If it's sealed or encapsulated, insulate the foundation walls and rim joists. Don't mix the two approaches.
Why is the insulation falling down in my crawl space?

Batts between floor joists often fall when their supports fail or when they get wet and heavy. Fallen insulation should be removed and checked for moisture, mold or pests before new insulation goes in with proper supports.
Can crawl space insulation reduce musty smells in my house?

Insulation alone won't. Musty smells come from moisture and mold. Fixing the moisture source, laying a vapor barrier, sealing the floor and sealing the ducts is what keeps crawl space air out of your home.
Do ducts in a crawl space need insulation?
Yes. Uninsulated ducts lose heat in winter, gain heat in summer and can sweat when cold air runs through them. Seal the joints first, then insulate.
